job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
• Executive finance leadership role
  • Purpose-driven NFP connecting people to meaningful work
  • Bendigo based

About the organisation

CVGT Employment (CVGT) is a not-for-profit, for-purpose organisation that has connected people to meaningful work since 1983. It was established as the Central Victoria Group Apprenticeship Scheme in response to youth unemployment in the Bendigo region. Since then, this organisation has become a trusted provider of employment services, apprenticeships and traineeships across Victoria, southern New South Wales and Tasmania. Operating from around 90 locations, CVGT supports over 20,000 people annually. The organisation is committed to inclusive employment solutions that benefit individuals, businesses and communities, guided by its values and strategic plan, which focus on delivering meaningful social, community and organisational impact.

About the role

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is responsible for leading CVGT's financial strategy, reporting, treasury and investments, governance frameworks and organisational performance analysis. The role translates complex financial information into practical insights that support informed decision-making, strengthen organisational resilience and enable effective service delivery across a dynamic and evolving funding environment. As a key member of the Executive Management Team, the CFO will work closely with leaders across the organisation to understand the business, provide thoughtful commercial and financial counsel, and contribute to strategic priorities across growth, innovation and organisational performance.

This is a highly trusted executive leadership role that combines sound financial stewardship with commercial acumen, future-focused thinking and a collaborative approach. The CFO will play a critical role in supporting the CEO, Board and Executive team to ensure CVGT remains financially strong, adaptable and well positioned to deliver on its purpose and strategic ambitions.

About you

CPA or CA qualified, you are an accomplished senior finance leader with experience partnering with CEOs, Executive Teams, Boards and Board Committees. You bring strong expertise across financial stewardship, investments and governance, together with the commercial acumen to support strategic decision-making and organisational performance. A strategic yet pragmatic thinker, you can develop robust financial models and business cases, translate complex financial information into clear insights, and contribute confidently at board and executive level. You have the credibility to respectfully challenge thinking, encourage open discussion and constructive debate, and build trusted relationships across the organisation. An engaging people leader, you have a track record of developing high-performing teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. You combine sound judgement, integrity and a collaborative approach, providing trusted advice that supports sustainable growth, organisational resilience and the achievement of CVGT's strategic objectives.

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Jacinta Maguire at SHK via email at jacinta.maguire@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3710933. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Senior Director Research Security, Ethics & Integrity
job.description:
• Lead compliance across research security and integrity
  • Major research-intensive organisation
  • Safeguard trusted, high-impact research

About the organisation

This large, research-intensive Australian organisation has a multi-division footprint and an extensive global network of research and industry partners. Its strategic plan focuses on expanding large-scale, challenge-driven research programs and industry partnerships that address major global challenges. Its approach relies on transdisciplinary teams and alliances across multiple sectors, both in Australia and internationally. The organisation is investing in internal research capability and coordination and in strengthening local and international partnerships. The Office of Research Ethics and Integrity provides professional support and advice on research ethics, integrity and compliance. It administers the organisation's ethics and compliance committees and maintains the research information systems that underpin institutional reporting.

About the role

The Senior Director, Research Security, Ethics and Integrity (Senior Director) will lead the organisation’s institutional approach to research security, research integrity, defence and sovereign capability, research governance and associated national security obligations. This includes strategic coordination of governance across the organisation, covering policy, compliance, risk assessment, education, operational oversight and external engagement. The Senior Director will oversee the Office of Research Ethics and Integrity, with two direct reports, a team of approximately 25 staff and a budget of up to $5.5m. The appointee will provide strategic advice to senior executives and governance committees on emerging geopolitical, foreign interference and regulatory risks. This includes overseeing complex and sensitive matters that require executive coordination. In building relationships with Commonwealth agencies, sector bodies and peer institutions, and national and international funder expectations will be translated into institutional policy, systems and practice. Key to success will be building a positive, enabling culture of research integrity and security across the organisation.

About you

You present with extensive senior leadership experience in compliance, research governance, research integrity, research security, national security or defence, preferably in higher education or a related sector, and hold a relevant postgraduate qualification, or an equivalent combination of experience and education. With a deep understanding of Australian and international frameworks for regulatory compliance, research integrity, foreign interference and defence research, you are well placed to give executive leaders and governance bodies authoritative strategic and policy advice on sensitive matters. Your experience leading multidisciplinary professional teams strengthens this advice. Quick to absorb new information, you turn it into practical solutions. Skilled at negotiating, influencing and building consensus among diverse senior stakeholders, you work effectively in politically complex environments. Within a large organisation, you set priorities, allocate resources and meet deadlines under pressure. This is a rare opportunity to set the standard for research security and integrity in Australia, protecting the trust that underpins high-impact research and giving a leading research organisation the confidence to pursue bold, globally significant partnerships.

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Andrew Richards at SHK on 0422 279 039 or via email on andrew.richards@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3708964. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

Applications close AEST 11.59pm on Friday 11th December 2026.

job.title: Director of Technology & Information
job.description:
• Influence the Dairy industry’s use of digital products and data
  • National, farmer-first industry organisation
  • Shape technology and data use across the dairy sector

About the organisation

Dairy Australia's vision is to be a leader in shaping a profitable and sustainable dairy industry. This organisation provides services that benefit and advance dairy farm businesses and the wider industry, including investment in research and innovation, learning and capability development, marketing, policy research, market insights and trade development. Dairy Australia operates nationally, with teams across Australia’s eight dairying regions and a central office in Southbank, Melbourne. The organisation's values – Farmer first, One team, Innovative thinking and Decisive action – guide its decisions and actions.

About the role

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and as a member of the Dairy Australia Leadership Team, the Director of Technology & Information leads the organisation's internal technology and data agenda, with four direct and eight indirect reports. Externally, the Director will work with DataGene (an independent, industry-owned organisation), dairy processors, other data holders and research and development corporations to build alignment on an industry data strategy and drive its implementation, including governance covering data access, quality, stewardship, privacy, security and responsible use.

The role offers direct influence over how the Australian dairy industry connects and uses its data, and over how contemporary and emerging technologies, including AI, are applied to research, innovation and the end-to-end dairy value chain. Internally, the Director is accountable for technology and data strategy, technology operations, cyber security, data governance, vendor management and the responsible adoption of AI, ensuring these capabilities are secure, reliable and aligned with organisational priorities. The role will work at the forefront of technology, data and AI, advising the Leadership Team and Board on relevant opportunities, risks and implications.

About you

Tertiary qualified in information technology, computer science, or a related discipline, you bring significant leadership experience in a senior technology, information systems or digital services role. You have developed and delivered technology strategies and roadmaps, led technology operations, infrastructure, enterprise applications, data and cyber security capabilities, and led major technology-enabled transformation or service delivery initiatives.

You have strong knowledge of cyber security, information governance, privacy, business continuity and technology risk, a sound understanding of cloud services and system integration, and the commercial judgement to manage budgets, investment portfolios, vendors and commercial contracts. Your ability to influence and advise Boards and senior leadership teams, negotiate with diverse stakeholders and explain complex technology matters clearly to non-technical audiences will be essential. This is a rare role for its ability to have sector-wide impact.

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Brian Barry at SHK via email at brian.barry@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3705475 (do not submit your application via email).

Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Applicants must hold full unrestricted Australian working rights and a driver’s licence to be considered for this role. Note: Shortlisted candidates will be asked to undertake a psychometric profile.

job.title: Head of Faculty, Screen & Stage
job.description:
• Lead national academic strategy across a premier creative industries institution
  • Build faculty profile nationally and internationally through executive-level industry engagement and strategic partnerships
  • Key member of the Academic Leadership Team based in Sydney

About the organisation

Founded in 1982, JMC Academy is one of Australia's largest private higher education providers and a leading creative industries institution. It offers accredited degrees and diplomas in film and television production, acting, entertainment business management, design, animation, game design and music production to about 2,500 students a year across its Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane campuses. With enviable QILT survey results, industry-standard facilities, sustained investment in emerging technologies and a global network of creative practitioners and industry partners, JMC provides students with a contemporary education that reflects the evolving needs of the creative economy. JMC is committed to delivering innovative, industry-connected learning experiences that equip graduates with the skills, capabilities and professional networks required to guide them into rewarding careers and make their own indelible mark on industry.

About the role

The Head of Faculty, Screen & Stage provides strategic academic, operational and commercial leadership for the Screen and Stage disciplines across JMC Academy's campuses nationally. Reporting to the Executive Dean and serving as a key member of the Academic Leadership Team, this newly created position will play a pivotal role in shaping the future direction, growth and reputation of the faculty. The Head of Faculty will drive excellence in teaching and learning, ensuring curriculum relevance and innovation, enhancing student outcomes and maintaining compliance with the TEQSA Higher Education Standards Framework. Leading and developing National Course Leaders and Department Coordinators across three campuses, the role will create and implements faculty strategy and collaboration across disciplines to support academic quality, growth and innovation. With responsibility for faculty budgets and commercial performance, the Head of Faculty will be accountable for achieving strategic, operational and financial objectives while building a high-performing and collaborative faculty culture. Externally, the role will lead institutional profile-building for the faculty and positions Screen & Stage competitively in a crowded creative education market. The appointee will cultivate and maintain executive-level relationships with industry and professional bodies through strategic collaborations, placement opportunities, MOUs and commercial projects. The Head of Faculty will also represent JMC Academy within key industry and higher education forums across Australia and internationally. Based in Sydney, the role requires regular travel to Melbourne and Brisbane.

About you

You possess significant current professional standing and industry credibility within one or more Screen and Stage discipline. Your substantial academic leadership experience, gained within a faculty, multi-campus or national higher education environment, is complemented by a postgraduate qualification, ideally at doctoral level. With a demonstrated record of leading teaching excellence, curriculum innovation, student success initiatives and digital transformation, you understand how to align academic quality with student engagement, graduate outcomes and organisational strategy. Commercially astute and strategically minded, you bring experience in managing budgets and financial performance together with a well-established executive-level industry network. Your success in developing strategic partnerships, industry alliances, placement opportunities and collaborative ventures has delivered measurable value for students, institutions and industry stakeholders. Rounding out your profile is a sound understanding of the Australian higher education regulatory environment and governance frameworks, including quality assurance and compliance requirements. A collaborative and authentic leader, you can inspire high-performing teams through periods of growth and change. You are excited by the opportunity to shape and strengthen a newly established faculty, and are committed to advancing JMC Academy's purpose, values and equity objectives.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
• Broad, transformative and commercial remit
  • ASX-listed property group with a great culture
  • Shape how communities live

About the organisation

The organisation is an ASX-listed developer and manager of residential communities with resort-style amenities. Headquartered in Melbourne, it has built a strong brand over more than two decades and has been shaped by a clear focus on customer experience. The business is maturing its corporate structure and has made tangible progress on a disciplined transformation agenda. It is strengthening its operating platform and positioning itself for sustainable growth, with a focus on customer outcomes, disciplined execution, efficiency, automation and better use of data. The culture is warm and collaborative. Benefits include an employee share scheme, a hybrid model with three office days and four additional paid days of leave each year.

About the role

Reporting to the CFO, the Financial Controller is a senior member of the finance function, with direct exposure to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team, Board and Audit & Risk Committee. The is a transformative and influential role far broader than a typical controllership. It covers financial control, statutory reporting, technical accounting, tax and audit, as well as budgeting, forecasting, and management and Board reporting. The Financial Controller will develop and deliver a finance transformation and systems roadmap, including the future of the ERP platform. This includes reducing manual and spreadsheet-based processes, improving data quality, and identifying practical uses of automation and AI. The Financial Controller will also present to the Board and lead a lean team with a mix of experience levels. Key to success will be bringing a fresh perspective, leading change within Finance and across the business, and turning financial information into clear, commercial insight.

About you

CA or CPA qualified ideally with a Big 4 or equivalent foundation, you are a senior finance leader with 15+ years' experience, including significant time in financial control or financial reporting. Listed company experience is preferred. You have deep technical accounting expertise and have managed complex accounting matters, statutory reporting and audit. You have led, or played a senior leadership role in, a significant finance transformation, systems implementation or reporting improvement program. Experience in property, development, real estate or asset management, including inventory and investment property, will be well regarded. You are curious, hands-on and comfortable challenging the status quo. You are also a developmental leader who brings people with you through change. You communicate clearly with executives and Boards, and you work in a collaborative, warm way that suits an organisation focused on its customers.

How to apply

job.title: Associate Director, Strategic & Capital Investments
job.description:
• Steward strategic and capital investment
  • Leading international research university
  • Resourcing education and research impact

About the organisation

Established in 1853, the University of Melbourne is a leading international university with a tradition of excellence in teaching and research. Its main campus in Parkville is the hub of a knowledge precinct that includes eight hospitals, many leading research institutes and a range of knowledge-based industries. Under Strategy 2030, this institution's purpose is to benefit society through the transformative impact of its education and research, supported by a resilient institution. Within the Chief Operating Officer Portfolio, the Chief Financial Officer Group ensures the University has the financial and physical resources to deliver its academic activities and remain sustainable on an intergenerational basis. Its Enterprise Planning Office partners with the University Executive and senior leaders to bring strategy, planning, budget and investment into a single, consistent process.

About the role

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Planning Office, the Associate Director, Strategic & Capital Investments stewards the University's strategic and capital investment pipeline and is the primary conduit between initiative sponsors and governance bodies. The Associate Director will develop and govern investment standards, including business case templates, assessment criteria and minimum evidence requirements, and will maintain the investment framework up to business case approval. This includes monitoring pipeline demand, timing and interdependencies, and preparing advice with the Director and the Chief Financial Officer on options, value for money, affordability, risk and benefits. Working with the Associate Directors of EPMO and University Planning, the Associate Director will also secure cross-functional input across finance, risk, estates, digital and HR, and lead the annual collation of the Capital Plan and Strategic Allocations. Key to success will be engaging sponsors early, routing proposals to the right level of approval based on risk and translating objectives into measurable financial and non-financial benefits.

About you

Degree-qualified in finance, commerce, economics, business, public administration or a related discipline, you have extensive experience in investment appraisal, business case development and portfolio-level investment governance in a large, complex organisation. A senior finance business partner by background, you bring expertise in financial modelling, cost-benefit analysis, affordability assessment, and funding and partnership models. You can move between detail and the big picture, translating operations and service delivery into financial and other benefits. You are credible with senior executives and sponsors, apply rigour to every dollar, and can say no constructively while keeping stakeholders engaged. Higher education experience is not essential. A strong understanding of mission-driven institutions will be well regarded.

job.title: Global Head of Growth
job.description:
• Leading regulatory growth consultancy and B2C technology start up
  • Own the entire marketing growth engine of an existing powerhouse and new tech platform.
  • C-suite scale up opportunity, backed by a reputable brand

About the organisation

This well-established, leading Australian-backed company is launching a new software platform that helps entrepreneurs start, run and grow businesses in regulated industries. By bringing business setup, licensing, compliance and growth tools into one place, the platform makes business ownership more accessible in markets traditionally difficult to enter, creating a significant opportunity for global expansion. With ambitious plans to establish a differentiated market position, build a recognised brand and expand globally, the organisation is entering an exciting phase of growth. This is an opportunity to join at a pivotal stage, shape the future direction of a new platform (and the existing company) and play a defining role in building a high-growth global technology platform.

About the role

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and indirectly to the Founder & CEO, the Global Head of Growth will own the end-to-end marketing growth strategy, with primary accountability for launching and scaling the new platform, as well as leading the company's existing marketing function. This is a strategic, commercially accountable leadership role spanning the entire customer journey, from market awareness and acquisition through to conversion, activation, engagement and retention. You will design and build the growth engine, encompassing paid and organic acquisition, funnel optimisation, lifecycle marketing, CRM, automation and customer experience. You will also shape brand positioning, messaging and category creation, establishing a compelling market narrative and creative direction across paid, organic, social and video channels. Leading a multidisciplinary team across campaigns, lifecycle, performance, social, video and PR, you will establish a high-performance growth culture, drive data-led decision-making and ensure marketing investment translates into measurable commercial outcomes. You will own analytics, attribution and performance reporting, bringing together strategic leadership with a hands-on approach to execution. This is fundamentally a builder role. The opportunity is to establish a scalable, commercially accountable growth engine, create repeatable acquisition and retention models, and develop the platform's presence in Australia and international markets.

About you

You are an accomplished B2C growth and marketing leader with a track record of building and scaling businesses in high-growth, performance-driven technology and/or large consumer branded product environments. You have been instrumental in taking a product, platform or brand from early-stage through to meaningful commercial scale, ideally within a technology, SaaS, digital platform or high-profile consumer business. Your experience combines strong B2C acquisition and brand-building capabilities with an understanding of B2B customer acquisition and commercial models. You have owned end-to-end growth strategies, including acquisition funnels, performance marketing, lifecycle, CRM, retention and brand positioning. You are equally comfortable developing a growth strategy, managing significant advertising budgets, analysing conversion data and rolling up your sleeves to execute. An experienced leader of multidisciplinary teams, you know how to build capability, establish accountability and create a culture of high performance and continuous improvement. You bring strong commercial acumen, analytical capability and a deep understanding of digital customer behaviour. Fluent in performance marketing, CRM, automation and emerging AI-enabled marketing tools, you have a strong appreciation for brand, creative and compelling storytelling. Above all, you are entrepreneurial, commercially driven and comfortable operating in an evolving environment. You thrive on building something from the ground up, move quickly from strategy to execution and have the ambition to take a new technology platform into new markets.

job.title: Head of Facilities and Asset Management
job.description:
• Lead whole-of-life portfolio stewardship
  • Not-for-profit, diverse services
  • Safe, welcoming places for community

About the organisation

Our client is a not-for-profit organisation providing residential aged care, retirement living, affordable housing, disability services, community services and specialist education. Its property portfolio supports people with diverse needs across metropolitan and regional locations. The portfolio includes operational facilities, homes, community settings, grounds and corporate workplaces. For this organisation, the condition, safety, accessibility and presentation of its properties are central to customer experience, service quality, operational continuity and long-term sustainability. Its work is guided by a clear set of values centred on love, joy, hospitality and courage.

About the role

As a member of the Leadership Team, the Head of Facilities and Asset Management will be responsible for the whole-of-life stewardship, presentation, safety, compliance and commercial performance of the organisation's property portfolio. The Head will lead a customer-focused facilities and maintenance function, setting portfolio-wide standards while building local accountability and partnerships with operational leaders. This includes shaping a rolling 10-year asset management and renewal plan, establishing the property and asset management system as the single source of truth for asset, maintenance and compliance information, and managing facilities and asset service contracts. The Head will also oversee property operating and capital budgets and the renewal and minor capital works program. They will bring environmental performance and climate resilience into asset planning, and work with the Head of Development to commission major developments and transition them into ongoing facilities management.

About you

You are tertiary qualified in property, asset management, facilities management, engineering, construction management, commerce or a related discipline, or have equivalent substantial experience. You bring 10 or more years of senior leadership in facilities, maintenance or asset management across a large, geographically dispersed and operationally complex property portfolio. You have led high-volume maintenance operations and built accountable, service-oriented teams. You also bring strong commercial capability across operating and capital budgets, whole-of-life costing, business cases, procurement, and the negotiation and management of complex outsourced contracts. Your experience with an integrated property and asset management platform and your knowledge of building, essential services, workplace safety, accessibility and statutory compliance obligations will help you improve maintenance control, data quality and reporting.

job.description:
• Leading Australian university, global footprint
  • Build new B2B enterprise-wide industry engagement function
  • Connect industry and government with research, education and innovation

About the organisation

This large Australian university has a global footprint and long-standing reputation for excellence in education, research and industry engagement. With multiple campuses, and an established international presence, it is committed to creating transformative experiences for students and making a meaningful impact through research, innovation and engagement. The university is now creating a dedicated and coordinated enterprise-level industry engagement function, aiming to invest in mutually beneficial collaborations, diversify revenue, give industry partners a coordinated and clear way into the institution, and support its long-term strategic objectives.

About the role

Reporting to the Vice-President, Engagement, the Executive Director, Industry Engagement will establish, scale and lead a newly created industry engagement function, aligned with the university's broader engagement strategy, research priorities and education ambitions. The role will drive a coordinated effort for identified priority areas and sectors to enable a more connected approach to industry engagement across the university. Establishing clear ownership of key relationships and enabling industry partners to navigate the university more easily, the appointee will foster a collaborative and a one-university mindset for industry engagement, balanced with faculty and portfolio objectives. They will position the university as a trusted partner for corporates, government, industry associations and professional bodies, across local and international markets by identifying, developing and managing relationships that create mutual value and commercial outcomes, through research collaboration, workforce development, innovation, philanthropy and graduate employability.

About you

You are a senior executive who has built and led B2B and/or B2G industry engagement, business development, sales or growth functions, within the higher education and commercial sectors ideally. Your experience may also span the government innovation ecosystem and STEM industries, and you have originated and closed large, complex commercial deals at scale enterprise wide. You think broadly across all partnership, growth and revenue opportunities, building credible relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. You can bring independent-minded senior leaders and academics together around large and complex shared opportunities and keep them aligned through to delivery. Analytical and commercially focused, you use data and market insight to build pipeline and prioritise effort, and you have championed CRM adoption across complex stakeholder groups. You have designed operating models and built high-performing teams in complex organisations, can negotiate with skill, and have represented an institution confidently in public and international forums. Experience in South-East Asian and European markets, and a commitment to both vocational and higher education, will be well regarded.

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Dalia Klein at SHK on 0401 000 499. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Applications close 5pm Sunday 29 Nov AEDT

job.title: Executive Director Marketing & Communications
job.description:
• Major Australian global university
  • Lead newly integrated marketing, communications and digital function
  • Transformative leadership opportunity

About the organisation

This organisation is one of Australia's largest and most internationally connected universities, with a global footprint spanning Asia and Europe. With a long-standing reputation for excellence in education, research and industry engagement, the university is known for its practical, outward-facing approach, working closely with industry, government and community partners to deliver real-world solutions and lasting social and economic impact. The university is committed to creating transformative experiences for students and making a meaningful impact, while offering a vibrant, inclusive workplace where innovation thrives, diverse perspectives are valued and people are empowered to shape a better future.

About the role

Reporting to the Vice-President, Engagement, the Executive Director Marketing & Communications will lead the integration of the marketing and communications function, bringing together global brand and marketing, communications, and digital & experience to deliver a unified strategic narrative, strengthen brand and reputation, drive a differentiated market positioning, and create seamless, audience-centred experiences across domestic and international markets. Leading the evolution of the university's engagement approach through contemporary marketing, communications and digital, the role will leverage data, insights, technology and customer-centred design to drive impact, inform decision-making, and enhance organisational performance. The appointee will ensure the university remains responsive to changing audience expectations, market dynamics and emerging opportunities in an increasingly competitive and volatile environment, and support university priorities, including revenue diversification, industry engagement, staff and student engagement, research impact, lifelong learning, philanthropy, alumni engagement and global positioning. Key to the role is embedding effective operating models and ways of working that strengthen collaboration, improve efficiency and maximise organisational impact, and driving a high-performing innovative team, empowered to deliver excellence and measurable outcomes that advance the university's strategic objectives and global reputation.

About you

You are a contemporary marketing, communications and digital leader with a proven record of leading multidisciplinary functions at scale in large, complex and high-profile organisations. Your experience is ideally within higher education or a relevant commercial services sector. You bring deep expertise in brand strategy, market development, audience engagement, CX, proposition development and campaigns, using data, insights and technology to drive measurable outcomes. You have led enterprise communications that strengthen reputation and build internal and external stakeholder trust, spanning strategic narrative, executive communications, media and government relations, issues management and crisis communications. Having integrated best practice marketing, communications and digital capabilities to deliver a coherent brand, unified audience experience and greater organisational effectiveness, you foster collaboration and harness digital platforms, emerging technologies and customer-centred design. An accomplished executive change leader, your influencing and stakeholder management skills enable you to advise, challenge and guide the Vice-Chancellor, university executive and senior leaders. With strategic, commercial and analytical acumen you can identify market opportunities, support revenue diversification and develop compelling value propositions and growth strategies. Your passion for leading and inspiring large-scale transformation and the design and implementation of operating models, positions you to shape the university's next chapter.

job.title: Group Manager, Enterprise Technology & Digital Enablement
job.description:
• Set enterprise technology direction
  • Shape technology in a commercially focused state agency
  • Foster business engagement and a high performing team

About the organisation

VicTrack owns Victoria’s rail land, infrastructure, and related assets, with an $88 billion portfolio. In addition to its ongoing asset custodian role, the organisation is transforming to be a more commercially driven business, pursuing new opportunities from its extensive asset base and strengthening its core role in Victoria’s transport system. With annual revenue at around $150 million and ambitions for significant growth, VicTrack is reshaping how it operates to meet its aspirations for the future.

About the role

Reporting to the Chief Enterprise Services Officer and sitting on the Enterprise Services Senior Leadership Team, you will be VicTrack’s most senior technology leader. You will be accountable for technology, digital capability, data management and cyber security across the internal operating environment, leading a team of approximately 30 spanning strategy and architecture, portfolio and business engagement, program delivery, enterprise applications, digital enablement, and technology operations and security. You will develop an enterprise strategy, a three-year integrated roadmap and costed annual plans, and establish transparent investment and portfolio governance, all while maintaining secure, resilient operations across critical infrastructure and telecommunications assets. You will also lead implementation of the future state operating model, reshape team capability and enable the responsible adoption of automation, data and AI. Key to success will be building business engagement and trust, and translating technology, commercial and risk matters into clear advice that supports investment decisions by the Executive Leadership Team and Board.

About you

You are a highly engaging senior technology executive with substantial experience leading enterprise technology and digital functions in complex, asset intensive, regulated or public purpose environments. Tertiary qualified, you have some direct prior experience in government, while bringing a well-tuned commercial mindset, with experience managing significant budgets, strategic sourcing, major vendor relationships and commercial contracts. You have governed cyber security, operational resilience and risk at enterprise level, and understand the obligations that come with critical infrastructure. You have led teams through change with openness, respect and emotional intelligence, and take calculated risks with sound judgement. As a member of a senior leadership group, you influence peers, executives and Boards, and hold your position constructively. Experience in transport, infrastructure or telecommunications will be advantageous. Motivated by VicTrack’s purpose, you want to build technology foundations that create lasting impact.

job.title: Executive Director, Transformation and Reform
job.description:
• Lead whole-of-enterprise transformation
  • Expanded powers and jurisdiction
  • Strengthen anti-corruption measures

About the organisation

The Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission (IBAC) works to expose and prevent corruption affecting all Victorians. Recent legislative reform has expanded IBAC's powers and jurisdiction, which requires new and strengthened capabilities. The organisation is focused on meeting those obligations, guided by the IBAC Strategy 2025–28 and a focus on responsiveness, enabling intelligence and people. IBAC's Executive Leadership Team works to a leadership charter built on mutual support and open discussion, with decisions made in the interests of the whole organisation.

About the role

A new role reporting to the CEO and sitting on the Executive Leadership Team, the Executive Director, Transformation and Reform will lead the enterprise-wide transformation of IBAC. The Executive Director will create the future-state vision and integrated roadmap, work with the CEO on the operating model redesign and personally lead the reform workstreams around it, from concept to delivery. The role will also establish and lead a small team, collaborate with and advise the executive on priorities, risks and trade-offs, and help develop new capabilities alongside the uplift of the existing skillsets. Key to success will be maintaining statutory functions throughout and handing reform outcomes to business owners with sustainable capability in place. This is a two-year fixed-term appointment.

About you

You are an accomplished executive who has led complex, organisation-wide transformation from strategy to implementation in public sector integrity, regulatory, compliance, investigative or oversight environments. You bring a deep understanding of government and its accountability frameworks, enabling you to deliver meaningful, sustainable change while maintaining operational effectiveness. Pragmatic and future-focused, you can navigate legal and statutory complexity, connect strategy with execution, and keep people engaged through change. You are a collaborative and trusted leader who values different perspectives, builds genuine partnerships, and contributes positively to executive decision-making. Motivated by public purpose, you will relish the opportunity to help shape IBAC’s future and strengthen confidence in Victoria’s integrity system.
